title: git init
definition: The command used to create a new, empty Git repository or reinitialize an existing one.
simpleExplanation: You have a folder on your computer full of code. Git is currently ignoring it. By typing `git init`, you awaken Git. It creates a secret hidden folder called `.git` that acts as the 'brain' and starts tracking your files.
realWorldExample: Starting a brand new web project from scratch on your local computer.

basic: What does `git init` actually do under the hood?
intermediate: If you delete the `.git` folder, what happens to your code?

answers.question: What does it do?
answers.answer: It creates a hidden directory named `.git` inside your project folder. This folder contains all the necessary metadata and object databases for version control.

answers.question: Delete .git folder?
answers.answer: Your code (HTML, CSS, JS files) remains perfectly intact! But your entire Git history (all past saves, branches, and commits) is permanently deleted. It just becomes a normal, untracked Windows/Mac folder again.

codeExample:
# Create a new folder for your project
$ mkdir my-awesome-app
$ cd my-awesome-app

# Tell Git to start tracking this folder
$ git init
# Output: Initialized empty Git repository in /path/to/my-awesome-app/.git/

# If you run 'ls -a' (list all files, including hidden ones),
# you will see the secret .git folder!
$ ls -a
# Output: .  ..  .git
